questions.q: If $p = 6$, $q = -3$, then the value of $p^3 - 3p^2 + 3p + 3q + 3q^2 + q^3$ is:
questions.explain: The expression can be rewritten by completing the cubes. $(p - 1)^3 = p^3 - 3p^2 + 3p - 1 \Rightarrow p^3 - 3p^2 + 3p = (p - 1)^3 + 1$. Also, $(q + 1)^3 = q^3 + 3q^2 + 3q + 1 \Rightarrow q^3 + 3q^2 + 3q = (q + 1)^3 - 1$. Adding both gives $(p - 1)^3 + 1 + (q + 1)^3 - 1 = (p - 1)^3 + (q + 1)^3$. Substitute $p=6$ and $q=-3$: $(6 - 1)^3 + (-3 + 1)^3 = 5^3 + (-2)^3 = 125 - 8 = 117$.
